quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When leaving a highway as part of a group, which formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is best for most group riding. But switch to single-file when turning, curving, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid hitting the animal.
Change lanes as fast as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to crash into another vehicle. A collision with another car is more dangerous than hitting a small animal.

questions.question: During the day, you should use your headlight on:

options.text: Alternating between high and low beam

questions.correctAnswerText: High beam
questions.explanation: Use high beam during the day to make other drivers see you better. Use high beam anytime you are not following or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Plan travel distances based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place less experienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan ride length and segments based on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Scratch and become brittle over time and need regular replacement
Should break away during a crash

questions.correctAnswerText: Scratch and become brittle over time and need regular replacement
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. Over time they scratch and become brittle. Replace them regularly to stay protected and comfortable.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Lean your shoulders to match the turn angle
Sit up as tall as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: Before turning, slow down by releasing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: You may need less space between you and the vehicle ahead if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead
Weather and traffic conditions are good

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are good
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in poor conditions. This includes slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or heavy traffic.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handlegrip in the direction you want to go
Press the handlegrip opposite to the direction you want to go

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlegrip in the direction you want to go
questions.explanation: To swerve, gently press the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left grip then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip then the left.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard ahead
questions.explanation: Group signals help riders communicate. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots
Invite other drivers to share your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from blind spots, wind blasts, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from using your lane and provide an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, but not when it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane do not have oil.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, but not when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips onto the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area still provides enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should ride:

options.text: In the left part of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest place when being passed. Riding toward the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash. Riding away from the passing vehicle may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: If bad road conditions mean you need more time to stop, you should:

options.text: Follow the vehicle ahead more closely.
Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
Have someone else operate your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Leave more distance between you and the vehicle ahead if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. If the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead clearly, or traffic is heavy, use at least a three-second following distance.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans into a turn. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward to make the motorcycle lean in that direction.

questions.question: When using the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually.
Use only two fingers to grab the brake.
Push down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp hard on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure slowly and smoothly, increasing the force as needed.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before each ride to stay safe. You should check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce the time it takes to respond. This is especially important when riding through areas where danger might appear.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Remain in first gear.
questions.explanation: Downshift through the gears with the clutch as you slow and stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, you should:

options.text: Move the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to move the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If the throttle is stuck, try moving it back and forth several times. If it does not free up, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then speed up and leave it behind. If a larger animal is in your way, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: During a slow, tight turn, the rider should:

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about hazards or road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually stronger than a car's headlights.
Usually the same strength as a car's headlights.
Usually weaker than a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually weaker than a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and produce less light than car headlights.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
Either the left or right side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out.
